title: Pulse-starvation induced latency spikes and cross-tenant fairness remediation
creator: Marcus Li
description: This ticket captures the investigation, short-term mitigations, and tracked action items following a capacity event where the continuous batcher entered repeated 'pulse starvation' windows causing bursty token emission, long tail latency spikes (>99.9th percentile), and observable cross-tenant unfairness. The incident surfaced after recent affinity scheduling changes and a dynamic coalescer timeout optimization rolled out in runtime-1.21.
incident_summary: Between 2026-03-03 09:12 UTC and 2026-03-03 11:04 UTC, we observed periodic 500–900ms tails on text-generation requests for certain routes. The system showed repeated short intervals where batch formation halted for 10–60ms and then drained multiple queued requests simultaneously, producing burst latency and a set of customers experiencing sustained degradation. Autoscaling did not trigger because underlying GPUs were not fully utilized; the problem was batching coordination rather than capacity exhaustion.
timeline: 2026-03-03 09:12 UTC: Paging triggered to on-call (runtime team)
2026-03-03 09:18 UTC: Initial hypothesis - scheduler jitter; rolled back coalescer timeout on a subset of nodes
2026-03-03 10:05 UTC: Temporary reduction in incidents on rolled-back nodes; other nodes still affected
2026-03-03 10:30 UTC: Identified correlation with affinity scheduling pilot (slot pinning) introduced in runtime-1.21
2026-03-03 10:50 UTC: Deployed a safety patch: enforce max-wait (30ms) per aggregator pulse and enable logging hooks
2026-03-03 11:04 UTC: Incident declared resolved for majority of traffic; follow-up investigation ticket opened (this ticket)
impact: Intermittent tail-latency increases affecting P99/P99.9 on generation routes (approx +350ms median increase for affected windows). Three enterprise tenants reported degraded SLAs and one internal canary produced noisy telemetry. No token corruption or data loss observed.
root_causes: Pulse-starvation pattern: distributed batch aggregators occasionally failed to trigger drain pulses due to coordinated timer drift under heavy small-request workloads

Affinity scheduling (slot pinning) with fine-grained slot fragmentation amplified starvation windows because requests destined for a pinned slot waited until the slot became active, creating micro-queues

A recent coalescer optimization reduced the default max-wait in some paths but introduced a fast-backoff that synchronized across workers — when combined with timer drift, this caused repeated freeze-and-drain cycles
Insufficient observability: lack of per-aggregator state metrics (pulse lag, consecutive-starvation-count) made early detection difficult
mitigations_taken: Rolled back the aggressive coalescer fast-backoff flag on 40% of cluster (canary) — immediate partial improvement
Implemented temporary enforcement of a conservative max-wait (30ms) at aggregator level to avoid long starvation windows
Added short-term logging for aggregator pulse timestamps and starve counts; dashboards created to show pulse-distribution per-region
Disabled affinity slot pinning for the pilot cohort for 24 hours to validate impact
action_items: A1: Add per-aggregator pulse metrics (pulse_ts, last_drain_dur_ms, consecutive_starve_count) and a dashboard. Owner: Aisha Kapoor. Due: 2026-03-21
A2: Implement jittered drain timers (randomized +/- 2-6ms) to avoid synchronized backoff across workers. Owner: Tom Barnes. Due: 2026-03-28
A3: Rework affinity slot pinning to avoid micro-fragmentation: introduce soft-pinning with spillover after 8ms. Owner: Elena García. Due: 2026-04-04
A4: Add a circuit-breaker that forces a forced-drain after two missed pulses (configurable). Owner: Marcus Li. Due: 2026-03-25
A5: Run a chaos test that simulates clock skew and high small-request rates to validate fixes. Owner: SRE team (lead: Priya Raman). Due: 2026-04-08
A6: Postmortem write-up and customer communication package for impacted tenants. Owner: Product (Samir Patel) + Support (Jenna Ortiz). Due: 2026-03-18
followups: Schedule a cross-team review (Runtime / Scheduling / SRE / Observability) after A1 and A2 complete
Add automated alert that fires when >5% of aggregators report consecutive_starve_count >=2 for 1 minute
Consider expanding batching unit tests to cover timer-synchronization scenarios
Track fairness regressions in the weekly reliability digest until no regressions for 4 weeks
